references.text: The immediate context: The master of the house shuts the door, and those who knock are not allowed to enter. Jesus elaborates here on the consequence of not striving to enter through the narrow door ([ref:Luk 13:25-27|Luke 13:25-27]).

Jesus' words in the Sermon on the Mount about the narrow gate and the narrow way that leads to life, and that few find it. This is a close parallel to the image of the narrow door in [ref:Matt 7:13-14|Matthew 7:13-14].
Jesus says that not everyone who says "Lord, Lord" will enter the kingdom of heaven. This emphasizes that many will seek to enter but fail ([ref:Matt 7:21-23|Matthew 7:21-23]).
Jesus calls himself the door for the sheep. Whoever enters through him will be saved. The door as a symbol of salvation is directly linked to Jesus' person ([ref:Joh 10:7-9|John 10:7-9]).

Jesus speaks about the great demands of following him – to carry one's cross and renounce everything. This elaborates what it means to "strive" (ἀγωνίζεσθε) to enter ([ref:Luk 14:25-27|Luke 14:25-27]).
Paul uses the image of an athletic contest (ἀγωνίζομαι) to describe the Christian's struggle and self-discipline to win the imperishable crown of victory ([ref:1 Kor 9:24-27|1 Corinthians 9:24-27]).

Paul describes his own spiritual struggle to grasp what he has been grasped by in Christ, and presses on toward the goal – a parallel to striving (ἀγωνίζεσθε) to enter ([ref:Fil 3:12-14|Philippians 3:12-14]).

Peter urges believers to make their calling and election sure, for then they will be granted rich entry into the Lord's kingdom. The image of "entry" corresponds with "entering" through the door ([ref:2 Pet 1:10-11|2 Peter 1:10-11]).
Wisdom speaks of those who seek her but do not find her – a parallel to "many will seek to enter and will not be able" ([ref:Ordsp 1:28-29|Proverbs 1:28-29]).
Paul urges Timothy to "fight the good fight of faith" (ἀγωνίζου), the same verb Jesus uses in Luke 13:24 about striving to enter through the narrow door ([ref:1 Tim 6:12|1 Timothy 6:12]).
The author of Hebrews urges believers to strive to enter God's rest, so that no one falls away. The theme of striving to enter is shared with Jesus' exhortation ([ref:Hebr 4:11|Hebrews 4:11]).
